newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia to sell new Kekwah crude by tender-source.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to sell new Kekwah crude by tender-source.

text.p: Malaysia's oil trading firm Petco has decided to sell the first cargo of its new Bunga Kekwah crude through public tender, an industry source said on Friday.
Petco, a unit of state-oil group Petronas, plans to issue the tender next week, the source said.
The company had been debating for several months whether to issue a tender as a way to introduce the crude, or to sell the crude through bilateral negotiations.
The tender will look to sell 200-300,000 barrels of the medium sweet crude for loading in the first half of August.
The details will only be confirmed next week, the source said.
Petco expects the crude to trade using Tapis APPI as a benchmark.
Production of the Bunga Kekwah crude field will start in July at around 20,000 barrels per day and output is expected to double by 2000.

Kekway has an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 36.5 degrees and sulphur content of 0.05 percent. The crude is expected to yield 40 percent of gas oil and 40 percent of low sulphur waxy residue.

The consortium developing the field is made up of Petronas Carigali, with 46.06 percent, Petrovietnam Exploration and Production with 12.5 percent, Canada's International Petroleum Corp with 26.44 percent and Sands Petroleum AB SAPEfb.S with 15 percent.
